definitions.explanation: So bright that it's difficult to look at directly.
Figuratively describes someone or something that shines impressively.

examples.japanese: まぶしくて{目|め}を{開|あ}けていられない。
examples.english: It's so bright I can't keep my eyes open.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}の{光|ひかり}がまぶしくて、カーテンを{閉|し}めた。
examples.english: The morning light was so bright that I closed the curtains.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}の{笑顔|えがお}はまぶしいほど{輝|かがや}いていた。
{若|わか}い{人|ひと}たちの{活躍|かつやく}がまぶしい。
examples.english: The young people's achievements are brilliant.

examples.japanese: ステージの{上|うえ}で{歌|うた}っている{彼|かれ}の{姿|すがた}がまぶしかった。
examples.english: His figure singing on stage was radiant.

notes:
Can also be written as {眩|まぶ}しい (with kanji).

COMMON PATTERNS:
・まぶしくて〜できない (so bright that one can't ~)
・まぶしいほど (so radiant that, dazzlingly)
・{目|め}がまぶしい (my eyes are dazzled)

FIGURATIVE USE:
Often used to describe someone who appears brilliant, impressive, or youthful - someone whose brilliance is almost intimidating to look at directly.

CONJUGATION:
・まぶしくない (not dazzling)
・まぶしかった (was dazzling)
・まぶしくて (dazzling, and...)
